quest.title: Underwater Nocturne
quest.description: In order to rescue the people of Petrichor, you follow the strange cat named "Osse" into the mysterious Faded Castle...
quest.rewards_formatted: Adventure EXP x250, Primogem x30, Mora x30000, Hero's Wit x2

chapter.title: In the Hall of the Sea King

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: It's the strange shiny fish again! Feels like it's been following us from outside all this time, how weird...

dialogues.speaker: Osse
dialogues.text: Paimon, have you witnessed so little of the world as to find such things strange? Are we not underwater? Is it not ordinary to see all manner of fish about?

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Eh? But this big guy looks anything but ordinary!

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: And this voice... I've heard it before...

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Seriously? You mean from the dream you had before?

dialogues.speaker: Osse
dialogues.text: *sigh* This part of the sea outside is like the castle, it belongs to the past. It is something that should have been forgotten...

dialogues.speaker: Osse
dialogues.text: If one ceaselessly calls out to a monster that has been blotted from memory, they might yet jump out and cause trouble.

dialogues.speaker: Osse
dialogues.text: It is wise to be cautious. It is for the best if we simply treat it as an ordinary fish.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: You make everything sound so scary, Osse! Are you just trying to creep us out or something?

dialogues.speaker: Osse
dialogues.text: I simply mean to avoid unnecessary complications. After all, our top priority is to retrieve the surface-dwellers' souls, no?

dialogues.speaker: Osse
dialogues.text: It just so happens there's a "blank score" before us. We simply need to use the music box to tune the Autoharmonic Reed Pipes on either side, and we can obtain it.

dialogues.speaker: Osse
dialogues.text: Give it a go.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Is this the stage you spoke of earlier, Osse? And are Paimon's eyes deceiving her, or is the mural on top moving? It's kinda spooky...

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: That "terrifying power" couldn't be escaping from here, could it? Osse?

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Hey! Osse! Ossssseeee! Are you spacing out?

dialogues.speaker: Osse
dialogues.text: Meeeow?

dialogues.speaker: Osse
dialogues.text: ...Ahem. My apologies. I was distracted for a moment.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Did you once perform on this stage? Is that why you're feeling, uh... nostalgic, or something like that?

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: That seems unlikely!

response.speaker: Osse
response.text: I might have, or I might not. It was all in the past either way. Utterly irrelevant...

response.speaker: Osse
response.text: What matters now is the scent of discord I smell in the air. As though some presence, one that makes me uneasy, once visited this place.

response.speaker: Osse
response.text: I fear that specifics may only be ascertained once we have performed the "score" here.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: There's one here too? Paimon didn't notice...

response.speaker: Osse
response.text: Well, you may have seen "scores" shaped like strings, but you have not seen those shaped like murals. One such is before you.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Oh! So the pictures are moving because it's actually a score?

response.speaker: Osse
response.text: Yes. Did we not find a "blank score" before? It is time now to perform it. Please, do the honors.

choices.text: Perhaps you were an audience member.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Oh! Good point!

dialogues.speaker: Osse
dialogues.text: You are the mistaken one. We should have assimilated into this new nation thousands of years ago, but it was you who warped them into puppets of ancient hate.

dialogues.speaker: Osse
dialogues.text: Whether that Phobos matter is true or false, as long as my will has not dissipated, your schemes will not succeed.

dialogues.speaker: Boethius
dialogues.text: Do you mean to say, then, that we should abandon our honor as Remurians and degenerate into mere base insects?

dialogues.speaker: Boethius
dialogues.text: How could I ever allow my kin to return to those bags of decaying flesh and become slaves to fa{RUBY#[D]Fortuna}te once more?

dialogues.speaker: Osse
dialogues.text: It seems that the millennia have not led you to accept Remuria's downfall. If anything, you have grown more obstinate still.

dialogues.speaker: Boethius
dialogues.text: Perhaps it is in our stubbornness alone that we are quite similar. I thought that the long years would have rendered you willing to once more stand by our side.

dialogues.speaker: Boethius
dialogues.text: You betrayed the tribe that birthed you... and you betrayed Remuria. You may have become the "Golden Hunter," but you cannot remove the brand of the Sebastos that marks you still. You will always be a Remurian.

dialogues.speaker: Osse
dialogues.text: Remurians have long ceased to exist... save in your delusions. The world of old has passed away.

dialogues.speaker: Boethius
dialogues.text: Of course, of course — or so it was meant to be. But now, the border between past and present has faded.

dialogues.speaker: Boethius
dialogues.text: If you insist on becoming the enemy of our ancient realm and sealing me once more in a cage buried beneath the waves, then those Fontainians you wish to protect — yes, all of Petrichor — shall be buried as one.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Huh? No way! We won't let that happen!

dialogues.speaker: Boethius
dialogues.text: That is not up to you, insolent savage! When that time comes, your lowly flesh will be rendered as dust, but your souls will join with ours, and take the next step of evolution.

dialogues.speaker: Boethius
dialogues.text: We shall bestow upon you eternal, resilient bodies, that you may never again suffer mortal pain. Hmph... Should you have words of gratitude, I will hear them.

choices.text: Why, thank you so very much.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: That's not something we'd be thankful for at all!

response.speaker: Osse
response.text: Just like those puppets who danced as you performed, those pitiable slaves and servants? Those poor children, everything was stripped from them, and you still speak with such conviction.

response.speaker: Boethius
response.text: All things have their price. Narrow personal opinions are but refuse to be discarded by a higher class of being such as I.

response.speaker: Boethius
response.text: Besides, as I see it, they are the ideal form of humanity, adhering unerringly to perfect order.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: You're absolutely nuts, and... and despicable too!

response.speaker: Boethius
response.text: Despicable? Hah! And what would you call what Cassiodor did to us thousands of years ago, then!? By comparison, this is nothing!

response.speaker: Boethius
response.text: Ah, ah, but patience! We should have a good, long talk, but not here, no. We shall speak beneath the deep waters, in the deepest bowels of our ancient realm — where everything began.

response.speaker: Boethius
response.text: The realm awakens, Cassiodor! You are the sole survivor of our fallen realm, the sole Remurian left with free will, and you have left us for far too long.

response.speaker: Boethius
response.text: You must return to us, and listen to the lamentation and anger of the long years. Perhaps then you shall be more receptive to my symphony, and to the arrangement of Phobos.

response.speaker: Boethius
response.text: I will await you in the royal city of Remuria, in Domus Aurea, where the Sebastos plied his melody. I will, of course, extend the appropriate hospitality to those souls from the present before your arrival.

response.speaker: Boethius
response.text: Should you still remain resolute when the time comes, their souls will naturally receive their release.

response.speaker: Boethius
response.text: And as for you... You are not part of Phobos's plan, and yet, the great symphony shall in no wise cast out any audience...

response.speaker: Boethius
response.text: Do enjoy the passing prelude I have prepared for you!

response.speaker: Boethius
response.text: If fortune proves favorable, we shall meet again...

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Guess we're heading to Domus Aurea next, so we can meet that rude guy, right? It's gonna be dangerous for sure, but...

dialogues.speaker: Osse
dialogues.text: I will continue to guide you. It is, after all, my homeland. Though it may have sunk to the very bottom of the sea, I remember its paths still, even after all these millennia...

dialogues.speaker: Osse
dialogues.text: ...Or so I believe.

choices.text: Just don't let us down when it counts...

response.speaker: Osse
response.text: Should we encounter difficulties, you may count on me. Do not forget that I am far stronger than an ordinary cat.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Y'know, every time Paimon remembers that you're actually an ancient person from thousands of years ago, it just feels wrong that we're calling you Osse... But your full name is way too long, so...

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Okay, let's just call you "Monsieur Os," then! What do you think? Is it polite enough?

response.speaker: Monsieur Os
response.text: A name to me is nothing more than a label, but as this represents your acknowledgment, Paimon, I will gladly accept it.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Hehe, let's move out! It wouldn't be too bad to keep your rude friend waiting, but the townspeople can't wait that long.

dialogues.text: "Not only do we have the same hardy skin, but in our veins flows the same divine essence. We share the same wisdom and melody — the same will."

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Wh—Whoa! Someone's coming out of the mural!
It has been too long, dear friend! How many years since that day? Five hundred? Thousands?
Still, time matters not to us at all. You may be in this small body now, but I recognized you in an instant.
Well? Are you tired of battle and have decided to take up rat-catching as a new hobby?

dialogues.speaker: Osse
dialogues.text: It's you...

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: And what is he exactly? A monster? A ghost? Or... could he be the real Dark Lord?
"Dark Lord"? Pah! Barbarians remain barbarians, I see. Ignorant even of their own ignorance.

dialogues.speaker: Boethius
dialogues.text: "Boethius of Remuria" am I, foremost Harmost of Phobos. You need not introduce yourselves — I have no interest in the titles peddled by primitives.

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: You know this rude fella, Osse?

dialogues.speaker: Osse
dialogues.text: I do not deny it, but...

dialogues.speaker: Boethius
dialogues.text: Need you be so formal, Cassiodor? Do our years of service under our Sebastos, our God King, matter so little to you?

dialogues.speaker: Osse
dialogues.text: The past is past. I do not know how you, whose soul has long been shattered, have manifested, but it seems that the chaotic "symphony" is your doing, and none other.

dialogues.speaker: Osse
dialogues.text: Cease! Return the souls of those who live in the present, and go back to the shadow, beneath the deep waters, to where you belong — this is my final warning to you.

dialogues.speaker: Boethius
dialogues.text: Oh, and what then? Will you continue wearing your mask of hypocrisy, traitor? Will you shut your eyes and ears for another millennium?

dialogues.speaker: Boethius
dialogues.text: But you have noticed, haven't you? Why my melody would break its bonds at this time, and affect the present.

dialogues.speaker: Boethius
dialogues.text: Why my strength has given me the might to open the gate to the deep waters, allowing me to manifest.

dialogues.speaker: Boethius
dialogues.text: The power of the sea surges, Cassiodor... The return of Phobos is imminent!

dialogues.speaker: Osse
dialogues.text: "Phobos"...?

dialogues.speaker: Boethius
dialogues.text: Yes! Indeed! Over these thousands of years, I have already bound my soul to the shattered Phobos...

dialogues.speaker: Boethius
dialogues.text: The omniscient enigma, the great power, is about to finally descend once again. And is this not the wish that we once failed to accomplish?

dialogues.speaker: Osse
dialogues.text: To repeat the past is to give the ancient tragedy an encore... nor have I ever wanted to sacrifice innocent lives.

dialogues.speaker: Boethius
dialogues.text: Is that so? Well, not that it matters, Cassiodor. The world you have defended is coming apart at the seams. The people of bygone times you see before you shall return to their rightful places.

dialogues.speaker: Boethius
dialogues.text: Fontaine's existence is a mistake — one we shall correct. When the oceans swallow it, Remuria shall rise above the sea once again, and its light shall shine over the land!

dialogues.speaker: Boethius
dialogues.text: You can bury the past, but you shall not erase us. One day, we of the past shall devour all. Your work will be for naught.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Well, that shut 'em up. What do we do now, though?

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: If we wanna save the souls of the townspeople, we're gonna have to head to that doomus aria of whatever that super rude, duper arrogant guy talked about, right?

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: As you might recall, we weren't invited...

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Since when have we ever needed invitations to crash some bad guy's party?

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Oh, right, but from what he said, he seems to have known Osse for a long time. Said they worked for the "Sebastos" or whatever...

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: We need to have a good talk before we go...

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: "Cassiodor."

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: Seems to be an ancient nation.

dialogues.speaker: Osse
dialogues.text: If you have anything you'd like to ask me, this time, I shall tell you all I know...

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: Tell us about Remuria...

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: That's where you and that rude fellow are both from, right, Osse?

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: We've heard that name before.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: That's true! We heard about Remuria back in the Fortress of Meropide. Apparently, it was ruled by a god named Remus.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: The stories said Remus rode his big ship around and conquered all of Fontaine... but that's as much as Paimon knows.

dialogues.speaker: Osse
dialogues.text: Very well. The story begins before the Court of Fontaine as you know it was born...

dialogues.speaker: Osse
dialogues.text: The Sebastos, Remus, founded a nation above the High Sea that is Fontaine, and the ancestors of the present-day Fontainians named him the "Dark Lord Remus" in their terror.

dialogues.speaker: Osse
dialogues.text: Before it sank, this body of water was part of the Great Fontaine Lake and the location where the capital of Remuria was sited. As such, these waters have the same properties as those of Fontaine.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Wait, so we're actually in the ruins of Remuria now?

dialogues.speaker: Osse
dialogues.text: Indeed. But where the tale differs from commonly-told history is...

dialogues.speaker: Osse
dialogues.text: The people of Remuria were not ordinary humans like the Fontainians. Rather, they were a new race, their bodies were cast of stone, with Ichor for blood.

dialogues.speaker: Osse
dialogues.text: The Sebastos gave us such bodies in the hope that we could escape our prisons of rotting flesh and fate.

dialogues.speaker: Osse
dialogues.text: His great vision was that we should all grasp the power of the Symphony and thereby escape the shackles of Fortuna, becoming the masters of our own destiny.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: So those stone statues we saw on the way here... those were your... kin?

dialogues.speaker: Osse
dialogues.text: Precisely so. I fear that they have long lost their free will, however, becoming mindless slaves, worse off by far than the humans of old, easily perishable though they are.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Wait, in that case, why are you a cat?

dialogues.speaker: Osse
dialogues.text: I am a cat... "for now." And one's will and soul are more important than one's body, are they not? Regardless, it was the Sebastos who gave me new life.

dialogues.speaker: Osse
dialogues.text: We once possessed all of the High Sea, countless cities and palaces, flowers, flowing wine... and yet, fate found us all the same.

dialogues.speaker: Osse
dialogues.text: After returning from the deepest depths of the sea, the Sebastos used Ichor to create imperishable bodies for the people, and still, the prophesied future did not change.

dialogues.speaker: Osse
dialogues.text: Our God King believed that it was because human souls could not escape the gravity of fate, and so he wrote the "Symphony," a music that could weave destiny.

dialogues.speaker: Osse
dialogues.text: He believed that through this he had found a way to resist fate, but instead that path led us into utter darkness, step by step.

dialogues.speaker: Osse
dialogues.text: And in the end, the entire kingdom sank beneath the waves, as though it had been smote by divine judgment...

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: No...

dialogues.speaker: Osse
dialogues.text: I fear that even he did not foresee such an outcome, though all the same, that is what happened.

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: So, tell us about your impudent friend...

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Right! And he called you "Cassiodor" or something, right? But aren't you called Ouran... Oura... something?

dialogues.speaker: Osse
dialogues.text: Just as I have traversed many bodies, I have had many names. Of course, this is all thanks to the Sebastos, who separated my soul from the Grand Symphony...

response.speaker: Osse
response.text: But back to Boethius... He was not always evil. He was once a noble Harmost of Remuria, and the sole survivor following the great catastrophe that befell.

response.speaker: Osse
response.text: The original purpose of the golden castellum was to unify our surviving kin and prevent the catastrophe of the rising waters from ever occurring again. But evidently, Boethius had his own designs...

response.speaker: Osse
response.text: While I and my companions ranged across the land, struggling mightily to contain the power of the primordial waters, he used his eloquent tongue to sway those who remained.

response.speaker: Osse
response.text: He initiated a fell ritual that aimed to restore the shattered "symphony" and revive the ruined realm. To this end, he did not hesitate to dissolve the will of our kin and plunder the souls of Fontainians everywhere.

response.speaker: Osse
response.text: Many rulers and nobles became his pawns, and polities newly-born lay on the brink of destruction.

response.speaker: Osse
response.text: To stop him, who had by now clearly become a monster, I could only forsake my name and become one who hunts phantoms, resisting him alongside the Fontainians.

response.speaker: Osse
response.text: Bitter was the conflict before we were at last able to seal both him and the sea that had devoured our nation.

response.speaker: Player
response.text: And that is why he names you traitor.

response.speaker: Osse
response.text: I followed the Sebastos precisely because he had shown me that golden dream, a land where prejudice and difference were no more, a land of justice and freedom.

response.speaker: Osse
response.text: But that was what it had become after Remuria sank... no more than a dream. I would rather be called a traitor than let Boethius trample on our ideals.

response.speaker: Osse
response.text: I swore upon fate that I would serve as the barrier between past and present. Thus did I become the spirit-keeper of our ancient land.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Guess Mr. Impolite's a pretty stubborn guy, huh? Even after being beaten up and sealed, he's still looking to break out and cause trouble...

response.speaker: Osse
response.text: I had thought that even if evil lingered in him, his soul had long been broken, and he would remain naught but discordant notes, a "symphony" plunged into strife.

response.speaker: Osse
response.text: I never thought that he would weave his shattered self into the "symphony" and thus gain mastery over it. The discord and dissonance that now emanate from these waters can be regarded as an extension of his power.

response.speaker: Osse
response.text: If we are to defeat him... I fear we must await the moment when all his soul fragments have gathered around one body.

choices.text: ...You weren't planning on puppeting one of us at some point, were you?

response.speaker: Osse
response.text: Meow? Meow meow?

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Whoa, who would've thought such a cute little cat would consider doing something so horrible? ...Hey, waitasec! That means that you aren't even a cute kitty in the first place!

response.speaker: Osse
response.text: #Well, be that as it may, {NICKNAME}, you are used to playing the courageous savior, are you not? I, too, play the role I know well... albeit in an unfamiliar form.

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: Let's hear about the symphony and "Phobos"...

dialogues.speaker: Osse
dialogues.text: Where should I even begin... The "Symphony" is human memory and persona woven into a melody through musical notation, creating a song in which human souls can dwell and have their wishes fulfilled.

dialogues.speaker: Osse
dialogues.text: In that way, to master the "Symphony" is to master "fate"... This is the secret that the Great Golden Bee Sybilla, the prophet who survived the previous cycle, imparted.

dialogues.speaker: Osse
dialogues.text: The Sebastos, who created the "Symphony," poured these melodies into the insoluble Ichor, in hopes that all might control their own fates through playing that music.

dialogues.speaker: Osse
dialogues.text: He overestimated us, I fear, for his deeds terrified us... The people could not bear the burden of fate, and they begged their god and superiors for guidance.

dialogues.speaker: Osse
dialogues.text: At the request of the people, the Sebastos wrote all melodies into the grandest of melodies. This new Symphony would bring us all the greatest of happiness — and its name was "Phobos."

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: But it did not bring what was promised...

dialogues.speaker: Osse
dialogues.text: Indeed. You saw how it all ended, didn't you?

dialogues.speaker: Osse
dialogues.text: Had the Sebastos's plan worked, the Symphony would have woven a melody of utmost gentleness for us all — an eternity that would last a thousand years and beyond. But something went wrong...

dialogues.speaker: Osse
dialogues.text: Besides the Sebastos himself, only said superiors, the Harmosts, could have changed Phobos's melody.

dialogues.speaker: Osse
dialogues.text: And Boethius... was once an excellent Harmost.

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: So, about the dreamscape I saw...

dialogues.speaker: Osse
dialogues.text: #Ah, yes, those were indeed the memories left by he whom I served, the Sebastos, the God King Remus. Though I do not understand how you were able to see them, {NICKNAME}...

dialogues.speaker: Osse
dialogues.text: But I do not think you need to worry. If this chaotic "symphony" was enough to control you, it would have done so long ago on the surface. But that has not happened, yes?

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Hmm. Speaking of which, why isn't Este affected? Is he just, uh, especially gifted?

dialogues.speaker: Osse
dialogues.text: I do have some idea, but it might be best to wait for the right time to speak of that.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Oh, here we go again with the cliffhangers... Just don't forget to tell us, alright?

dialogues.speaker: Osse
dialogues.text: #In any case, since you can see these things, {NICKNAME}, that means that some fragment of the Sebastos's will and memory remains in this underwater symphony.

dialogues.speaker: Osse
dialogues.text: Long millennia have I searched... and if you could touch some more of these memories, perhaps I may find the answers I have sought all this time...

dialogues.speaker: Osse
dialogues.text: The great waves could not hurt a god, even should their crests scrape the very skies. And yet, the Sebastos disappeared without a trace when our nation fell into the depths...

dialogues.speaker: Osse
dialogues.text: He would not have sat idly by as his nation and people drowned in blood... So where did he go? Or was his passing Remuria's true death knell?

dialogues.speaker: Black Screen
dialogues.text: You tell of the strange dream you saw before...

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: That's all for now. We can leave the rest for later.

dialogues.speaker: Osse
dialogues.text: Very well. If there is anything else you wish to know, do not hesitate to ask me.

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: Is this because of the Primordial Sea?

dialogues.speaker: Boethius
dialogues.text: Do even barbarians know of its existence nowadays?

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: How can you call it a mistake...?
